Multinomial logistic regression

Source: R/multinomial_reg.R
multinomial_reg.Rd

Fit crude, exposure-specific adjusted, or joint multivariable multinomial logistic models for an unordered outcome with three or more categories.

Usage

multinomial_reg(
  data,
  outcome,
  exposures,
  adjust_for = NULL,
  multivariable = FALSE,
  multivariate = NULL,
  model_stats = FALSE,
  format = c("flextable", "gt"),
  theme = "minimal",
  show_ref = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing the outcome and predictors.

outcome

An unordered factor outcome with at least three levels. The first level is the reference outcome category.

exposures

Predictor variables to report.

adjust_for

Optional covariates included but not reported.

multivariable

Logical; fit all exposures in one model.

multivariate

Optional alias for `multivariable`.

model_stats

Logical; return model-fit and sample-size statistics.

format

Output table format: `"flextable"` or `"gt"`.

theme

Table styling preset.

show_ref

Logical; display categorical predictor reference rows.

Value

A `gtregression` object containing a side-by-side table of outcome comparisons, fitted models, statistics, and one standard regression object per comparison in `$per_outcome`.

Details

Each odds ratio compares one non-reference outcome category with the first outcome level. Outcome categories are nominal: their order has no numeric or severity interpretation. Use `relevel()` before fitting to choose another reference category.

Examples

set.seed(1501)
example_data <- data.frame(
  destination = factor(sample(c("Home", "Rehabilitation", "Hospital"), 120,
                              replace = TRUE),
                       levels = c("Home", "Rehabilitation", "Hospital")),
  treatment = factor(sample(c("Control", "Intervention"), 120, TRUE)),
  age = rnorm(120, 65, 10)
)
multinomial_reg(
  example_data,
  outcome = destination,
  exposures = treatment,
  adjust_for = age
)
